reasons.detail: R1 — Finalize-cleanup writes are redirected via `FinalizeCleanupPathResolver` and `recordFinalizeCleanupPostCommandMetadata` to main-repo durable paths, and plugin artifact/root flow context is shifted away from the target worktree.

R2 — Retained cleanup metadata is written by `recordFinalizeCleanupPostCommandMetadata` before final flow bookkeeping/commit in teardown, with durable owners for non-main-flow surfaces and durable sidecar/runtime-log paths used where appropriate.

R6 — Dispatcher runtime-log completion and finalize-cleanup agent metrics now persist through the shared post-command metadata recorder targeting external durable storage rather than mutating committed `flow.json`.

R5 — `recordFinalizeCleanupPostCommandMetadata` preserves report, plugin warning/follow-up, and recovery data in `callerVisible` and marks durable owners as observable so these artifacts remain accessible after relocation.

R3 — The diff adds a `force` path in `removeWorktreeForCleanup` that issues `git worktree remove --force` and wires `ctx.force` from `senti flow run finalize-cleanup` into teardown. New tests explicitly validate that forced runs call `worktree remove --force` for cleanup and that submodule-related forced failures do not fall back to non-force dirty-halt status logic.
R4 — Tests now cover cleanup-metrics sidecar appends, durable retained surfaces, normal worktree removal, feature branch deletion, and forced dirty worktree cleanup paths.
